comparisons.peer_topic: Stock-based compensation valuation models and expense recognition policy
comparisons.peer_summary: The Company uses the Black-Scholes and Monte Carlo simulation models to estimate the fair value of stock options, RSUs, and ESPP shares at the grant date. Compensation expense is generally recognized using the straight-line method over the vesting period, with forfeitures estimated at grant and revised if necessary.
comparisons.comparison: Both Broadcom and AMD estimate forfeiture rates at the time of grant and revise these estimates in subsequent periods if actual forfeitures differ from the original estimates, thereby adjusting the recognized compensation expense. Broadcom explicitly states that changes in estimates have a significant effect on expense and are recognized in the period of change. AMD similarly notes that forfeiture rates are estimated at grant and revised if necessary.

sentences.text: We will recognize additional expense if actual forfeitures are lower than we estimated, and will recognize a benefit if actual forfeitures are higher than we estimated.

Changes in the estimated forfeiture rates can have a significant effect on stock-based compensation expense since the effect of adjusting the rate is recognized in the period the forfeiture estimate is changed.
Forfeiture rates are estimated at the time of grant and revised, if necessary, in subsequent periods if actual forfeitures differ from those estimates.

comparisons.peer_topic: Share-based compensation amortization and tax asset elimination
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel uses the straight-line amortization method to recognize share-based compensation expense over the service period, net of estimated forfeitures. Upon exercise, cancellation, forfeiture, or expiration of stock options or vesting/forfeiture of RSUs, deferred tax assets are eliminated on a first-in, first-out basis for options and RSUs with multiple vesting dates.
comparisons.comparison: Both Broadcom and Intel recognize share-based compensation expense net of estimated forfeitures. However, Intel explicitly uses the straight-line amortization method to recognize this expense over the service period, whereas Broadcom's disclosure focuses on the estimation of forfeitures and the timing of expense adjustments without specifying the straight-line method in the provided text. Both companies adjust for actual forfeitures differing from estimates.

comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting for forfeitures of stock-based awards
comparisons.peer_summary: The company accounts for forfeitures of stock-based compensation as they occur rather than estimating them.
comparisons.comparison: Broadcom and Micron differ significantly in their treatment of stock-based compensation forfeitures. Broadcom estimates forfeiture rates and recognizes expense only for awards expected to vest, adjusting the expense in the period the estimate changes if actual results differ. In contrast, Micron accounts for forfeitures as they occur, rather than estimating them at the grant date.
